purpose: 300 distinct multi-node route-trace UI combinations; planning only.

recommended_fixture.reuse: Existing ten-node full-scale/1M demo on8883; no regeneration.
recommended_fixture.archive: Reuse the archive selected by the running launcher; do not replace or regenerate it.
recommended_fixture.verify: Observe actual device count,32 advertised route scenarios,capture vector and trace budgets. Missing live capabilities produce blocked records, never invented controls.

ordered_UI_actions: Open entry URL in executor's separate tab; wait for actual startup completion. Record offered scenarios/devices and advertised limits.
Ensure all available device checkboxes are checked. Select all is a toggle that clears selection when all are already checked: inspect first and activate only when needed.
Set relative_to_watermark time basis, offset0, strict clock policy; retain and record offered default topology intent/status perspective.
Click Reconstruct fabric if baseline controls/membership differ; wait for settled reconstruction and coverage. Do not treat initial loading as completion.
Clear device search; choose Highlight all, Underlay and Elements Compact; clear route-table filters; dismiss inspectors.
Apply each record's scenario/direction setup and restore advertised budgets; use observed/default steering unless a case explicitly selects a forced profile.
Reuse baseline reconstruction only if applied membership/time/projection are unchanged; each record still executes and records its own actions.

execution_rules: All records begin not_run. A plan, API response or function probe is not executed UI coverage.
Use observed DOM and normal browser input only; no application internal state, injected options or API substitution.
Resolve descriptive targets from live UI; record actual selected row/candidate/transition identity. Required missing content is blocked/not_applicable, not passed.
Record one individual settled outcome with each expected assertion evaluated; adapt selectors only to observed UI and document adaptations.
Repeat recovery after failures. New findings get related extension checks with separate IDs outside M001..M300.
Record wall timing and progress separately from browser tool overhead; no CPU claim is implied.
Return scenarios may use independent context. Assertions apply to requested/declared behavior, not assumed protocol success.

result_record_schema.actual_outcome: settled direction,outcome,path counts or exact error
result_record_schema.timing: UI wall timing, explicitly not CPU

cases.title: Single-active primary with eligible standby / bidirectional

setup.declared_semantics: Alpha selects one programmed path while retaining the alternate ambiguous boundary candidate as an inspectable inactive standby.
ordered_UI_actions: Select Trace scenario (#mn-route-scenario) option single-active-primary.
Select Directions to trace (#mn-route-validation) option bidirectional.
Open Advanced trace options; click Restore trace limits (#mn-route-restore-limits).
Select Missing-hop policy (#mn-route-policy)=strict; choose Focused path ([data-route-graph-mode=focused]).
Click Trace route (#mn-route-run).
Wait for the submitted trace to settle: run enabled and a current result or explicit error, with loading finished. Record errors as outcomes rather than success.
Record #mn-direction-comparison, #mn-route-summary, #mn-route-hopline, #mn-route-findings, direction tabs, selected path and observed focus.
Select Return ([data-route-direction=reverse]); record directional goal, hop sequence and findings.
Select Forward ([data-route-direction=forward]); record restored directional goal and selected path.
expected_assertions: Only requested directions have usable results; absent directions must not inherit previous traces.
Graph, hop sequence, summary and findings agree on the current endpoint goal.

Compare only applicable requested directions with the declared scenario behavior: Alpha selects one programmed path while retaining the alternate ambiguous boundary candidate as an inspectable inactive standby.
Delivery, incomplete/unknown evidence, consistency findings and failure remain separate facts; do not infer success merely from a drawn path.
No stale result, direction, packet inspector, or finding from another trace is presented as current.
reset_strategy: Dismiss inspectors using Escape; clear route-table filters and device text search.

Restore all available devices, relative watermark offset 0, Strict clock policy, Underlay, Compact elements, observed/default steering and advertised trace budgets. Reconstruct if topology controls changed.
Verify B0, then perform the next case's setup; reuse a reconstruction only when its recorded membership/time/projection is unchanged.

ordered_UI_actions: Select Trace scenario (#mn-route-scenario) option packet-forced-steering.
Select Directions to trace (#mn-route-validation) option bidirectional.
Open Advanced trace options; click Restore trace limits (#mn-route-restore-limits).
Select Missing-hop policy (#mn-route-policy)=strict; choose Focused path ([data-route-graph-mode=focused]).
Inspect Steering profile (#mn-route-steering); select advertised Observed plug-in decision (observed). Do not inject an unavailable option.
With advertised Observed plug-in decision (observed) selected, click Trace route (#mn-route-run); wait for the current request to settle.
Record forward observed hop sequence, candidate count, packet transition count and provenance; select Return and record the corresponding reverse evidence.

In Advanced trace options select the advertised Force alternate path through P2 (force-alternate-p2) in #mn-route-steering. If the profile is not offered, record the missing capability instead of inventing a candidate.

Click Trace route; wait for the current request to settle. Select Forward, then Return, and record each hop sequence, packet transition count, counterfactual badges, forced transition actor/origin and rule provenance.

Restore Observed plug-in decision (observed), click Trace route, and wait for the current request to settle. Select Forward and Return again; record restored paths and absence of stale forced-result provenance.
expected_assertions: Observed forwarding has one path per direction: node-a → transit-p-1 → transit-p-2 → node-b, with the reverse sequence for Return; four packet transitions and no user-forced counterfactual claim.

Forced P2 is a separate submitted trace input with one path per direction: node-a → transit-p-2 → node-b and the reverse sequence. The swap step is omitted, leaving push, PHP and delivery transitions.
Forced results remain explicitly counterfactual, with user-forced transition origin and rule provenance. Simulated delivery must not be presented as observed forwarding truth.
Returning to observed restores both original directional paths and four transitions; forced wrappers, rule badges, stale packet selections and preview highlights do not survive as current evidence.
This is one stateful observed-to-forced-to-observed combination; it does not test selection among simultaneous alternative candidate tabs.

setup.declared_semantics: A tenant IPv4 packet is wrapped by Ethernet/VXLAN/UDP/IPv6 and then carried inside an MPLS L3VPN transport, demonstrating multiple nested wrappers without protocol branches in core.
ordered_UI_actions: Select Trace scenario (#mn-route-scenario) option packet-vpn-over-vpn.
Select Directions to trace (#mn-route-validation) option bidirectional.
Open Advanced trace options; click Restore trace limits (#mn-route-restore-limits).
Select Missing-hop policy (#mn-route-policy)=strict; choose Focused path ([data-route-graph-mode=focused]).
Click Trace route (#mn-route-run).
Wait for the submitted trace to settle: run enabled and a current result or explicit error, with loading finished. Record errors as outcomes rather than success.
Hover the first actual packet transition chip (#mn-route-packet-rail [data-route-packet-ref]); inspect preview.
Click that same chip; record before/after layers, size bases, constraints and provenance in #mn-route-packet-detail.
Press Escape; record inspector dismissal and focus restoration.
Record #mn-direction-comparison, #mn-route-summary, #mn-route-hopline, #mn-route-findings, direction tabs, selected path and observed focus.
expected_assertions: Preview/pinned detail corresponds to the selected actual transition and declared step association.
Packet layers, size contracts and completeness are not inferred from protocol names.
For MTU fixtures, equality fits, incomparable contracts remain unknown and a declared drop stays distinct from delivery; apply only the selected fixture's semantics.
Mode/direction/retrace changes retire stale packet selection and detached highlights.
No stale result, direction, packet inspector, or finding from another trace is presented as current.
reset_strategy: Dismiss inspectors using Escape; clear route-table filters and device text search.

Restore all available devices, relative watermark offset 0, Strict clock policy, Underlay, Compact elements, observed/default steering and advertised trace budgets. Reconstruct if topology controls changed.
Verify B0, then perform the next case's setup; reuse a reconstruction only when its recorded membership/time/projection is unchanged.

setup.declared_semantics: A tenant static route recursively resolves a BGP next hop, an IS-IS transport path, and PE-E's external attachment.
ordered_UI_actions: Select Trace scenario (#mn-route-scenario) option recursive-static-to-external.
Select Directions to trace (#mn-route-validation) option bidirectional.
Open Advanced trace options; click Restore trace limits (#mn-route-restore-limits).
Select Missing-hop policy (#mn-route-policy)=strict; choose Focused path ([data-route-graph-mode=focused]).
Click Trace route (#mn-route-run).
Wait for the submitted trace to settle: run enabled and a current result or explicit error, with loading finished. Record errors as outcomes rather than success.
Record default-budget outcome and endpoint/profile fields.
Fill Maximum hops=0 and click Trace route; record browser validation/error without claiming a trace ran.
Fill Maximum hops=1.5 and click Trace route; record fractional validation.
Restore hops to its advertised default; fill recursion to observed max+1 and submit; record validation.
Click Restore trace limits; verify endpoints, scenario, direction and steering are unchanged and no automatic trace runs.
Click Trace route (#mn-route-run).
Wait for the submitted trace to settle: run enabled and a current result or explicit error, with loading finished. Record errors as outcomes rather than success.
Record recovered outcome and cleared restore reminder.
expected_assertions: A traversal bound cannot manufacture endpoint delivery; any stopped trace preserves its incomplete/limit reason.
Zero recursion is a valid advertised current bound, not an invalid-input test; nonrecursive scenarios may remain successful.
Invalid bounds are rejected without passing an old result off as a new successful trace.
Restore uses advertised defaults and successful explicit retry recovers without stale errors.
No stale result, direction, packet inspector, or finding from another trace is presented as current.
reset_strategy: Dismiss inspectors using Escape; clear route-table filters and device text search.

Restore all available devices, relative watermark offset 0, Strict clock policy, Underlay, Compact elements, observed/default steering and advertised trace budgets. Reconstruct if topology controls changed.
Verify B0, then perform the next case's setup; reuse a reconstruction only when its recorded membership/time/projection is unchanged.

Click Trace route (#mn-route-run).

Click Trace route (#mn-route-run).
Wait for the submitted trace to settle: run enabled and a current result or explicit error, with loading finished. Record errors as outcomes rather than success.
Record recovered outcome and cleared restore reminder.

cases.title: Single-active primary with eligible standby / combined-forward-filters

setup.declared_semantics: Alpha selects one programmed path while retaining the alternate ambiguous boundary candidate as an inspectable inactive standby.
ordered_UI_actions: Select Trace scenario (#mn-route-scenario) option single-active-primary.
Select Directions to trace (#mn-route-validation) option bidirectional.

Select table VRF=default, family=mpls_labeled_unicast, type=mpls_transport; select the observed node of a matching forward row; expand that node group.

Click Trace route (#mn-route-run).
